page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized server instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, translating to a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance contains 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show strong single-core capabilities, with the Geekbench single-core score of 2319.0 and Geekbench text processing score of 2868.0 both ranking in the top tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also demonstrate strong performance in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-bound metrics show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU score fall into the bottom 25%, while the Passmark memory score of 1085.12 is in the bottom 10%. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is also weak at 38.47 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highcpu-4 offers a specialized hardware profile that minimizes memory overhead to reduce costs for compute-bound tasks. It features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for cryptography and integer operations. Due to the low memory-to-CPU ratio and weak multi-core scaling, this instance is best suited for single-threaded processing, lightweight web serving, text processing, and basic utility workloads rather than memory-intensive databases or large-scale multi-threaded applications.
